violated_assumptions: Defect assumes JSON field should only accept JSON objects/arrays, not plain strings

source_grounding.call_chain_traced: REST v2 insert → checkAndSetData → DataType_JSON case accepts both gjson.String and gjson.JSON → plain string converted to []byte and stored
source_grounding.note: Source code reveals JSON field intentionally accepts multiple input types: plain strings (gjson.String) get converted to bytes, JSON objects (gjson.JSON) get their Raw value stored. This is by-design flexibility, not a defect.

falsification.observed: Query returns meta='plain_string' as-is, confirming the system accepts and stores plain strings in JSON fields by design

excluded: JSON fields in Milvus can store any JSON-serializable value including plain strings
REST API provides flexible JSON field handling

cognition_match.note: While this touches JSON field semantics, it doesn't match documented rejection patterns - plain strings in JSON fields appear to be intentionally supported

verdicts.rationale: The claimed defect (plain string rejected when inserting into JSON field) is FALSE_POSITIVE. Source code analysis (utils.go DataType_JSON handling) reveals intentional support for both plain strings and JSON objects in JSON fields. Live reproduction confirms insert with meta='plain_string' succeeds and stores the value as-is. JSON fields in Milvus are designed to store any JSON-serializable content, including plain strings, making this expected API behavior rather than a defect.
